_what_this_is: EVERY DURATION IN THE LADDER, AND WHAT EACH ONE CONTAINS. harness/budget.py computes
budget = ceil(p100(total_seconds for a scope) * headroom / 60) * 60, and harness/ci.py,
harness/static.py, harness/unit.py, harness/mutations/run.py,
harness/factory_mutations/run.py, harness/observe.py, harness/post_merge.py,
scripts/factory_evidence.py, scripts/factory_evidence_spine.py,
factory_kernel/runtime.py and factory_kernel/worker_runtime.py all read their timeouts
from that derivation instead of carrying a literal.
Every scope also declares WHAT RUNS INSIDE IT. harness/budget.py:validate() refuses a
record in which a wrapper's budget is smaller than the sum of the budgets it contains,
so raising an inner budget past its wrapper fails the suite -- and every gate that loads
this file -- in the change that raises it. That rule is the D-075 half. The D-073 half is
that a number without a recorded observation behind it cannot exist here at all.
kind='measured' is a wall clock somebody read off a real run. kind='projected' is
composed from measured parts, or preserves an inherited bound nobody has measured yet,
and says so in `source` with the parts. A projection is a placeholder for the first real
measurement, not a substitute for it: the runners print MUTATIONS_SECONDS /
FACTORY_MUTATIONS_SECONDS, per-defect MUTATION_TIMING lines and RUNG_SLOW warnings, so
real runs replace these entries with observations.
`contains` counts a scope ONCE when its clock shares this scope's deadline (one static
check inside the static rung, one focused test file inside the factory family): the inner
number names which step hung and can never outlive the wrapper. `bounded_seconds` is
contained work whose deadline is set somewhere else and is added as it stands.
`unbudgeted_seconds` is a measurement of contained work with no deadline at all, so it is
the one part that gets the headroom.

static-rung.what: The static rung: ruff lint, ruff format, mypy, tsc and biome.

harness/static.py -- one deadline shared by all five checks, each given what is left

unit-rung.what: The unit rung: backend pytest, frontend vitest and the factory trust-root suite.
applied_by: harness/ci.py run('unit', ...) -- the subprocess timeout on harness/unit.py
harness/unit.py -- one deadline shared by all three suites, each given what is left

quick-gate.what: One whole `python harness/ci.py --quick`: the static rung and the unit rung, and nothing below them.
applied_by: factory_kernel/runtime.py -- the build's quick gate and the re-head's quick gate

No run has yet reported the halves separately, so each half carries the pair's total until one does.

measurements.source: The widest of the four channels is the quick gate, measured at 179.027 s, 203.383 s and 207.4 s on three ubuntu runs (34066408781 rehead-quick-gate, 34061371205 quick-gate, the quick-authority job of 34066129225); p100 207.4 s. The recorded total is 520 s rather than 207.4 s so the derived budget (780 s) covers what the child's OWN static and unit rungs allow (360 + 360 + 30): a channel that killed `ci.py --quick` before its rungs did would report a timeout that is not the gate's.

measurements.environment: maintainer Windows host (per-file measurement), four concurrent copies
measurements.source: 391 defects across the eight manifests, one copy each, four concurrent. Per-file wall clock of the whole 72-file focused suite measured on 2026-09-07 at origin/main 6a7f8c6: 235.3 s total, median 0.59 s, p90 7.81 s, max 60.7 s (test_factory_bootstrap.py). Stopping at the first red in cheapest-first order gives an expected 30.3 s per caught defect against that distribution; 391 * 30.3 / 4 = 2962 s.
measurements.note: Without the reduction the same catalogue is 391 * 235.3 / 4 = 23,000 s (383 minutes) on that host. The catalogue is 406 defects as of this change; the projection is not re-derived here because it is due a real measurement, not a better estimate.

measurements.environment: ubuntu-24.04 GitHub-hosted runner, 4 vCPU (the validation host)
measurements.source: 2674 s application family + 2962 s factory family = 5636 s, raised to 5700 s so that the derived budget (8580 s) covers the two families' own budgets (4020 + 4500 = 8520 s), each of which is rounded up to a whole minute independently. The D-073 record derived 8460 s from the 5636 s sum, which was 60 s LESS than the two budgets it contains -- the same defect one level down.
measurements.note: The 900 s literal this replaced was never measured. Run 34066724127 (PR #134) passed security, provenance, all five judges, static, unit, the browser journey and the holdout, then died on 'TIMEOUT after 900s / GATE_FAILED: mutations' while still inside the application family.

measurements.environment: ubuntu-24.04 GitHub-hosted runner, 4 vCPU (the validation host)
measurements.source: The work itself is measured: run 34112301646's evidence stage reached these same three checks and refused in 0.395 s, and the provenance-fetch scope shows one `gh` call on this runner at 0.36 s. What is not measured is the worst case of a single GitHub API call, which is why this is a projection and not a reading: 60 s is two orders of magnitude above the observed work, so the derived 120 s bounds a stalled API call rather than a slow diff.
measurements.note: Replaces the literal `timeout=120` this stage was introduced with (D-077). Replace this projection with a p100 over the first ten runs that record the stage.

_raise_this: By recording the run that justifies it, in the same reviewed change -- and by raising every wrapper that contains it in that same change, because harness/budget.py refuses a record whose wrappers no longer bound their parts. A budget raised without a measurement behind it is the literal this file exists to retire; a wrapper left behind when an inner budget grows is the timeout that ended run 34081507222.
_the_one_wrapper_this_record_cannot_clos: dark-factory-worker.yml's `timeout-minutes: 300`. A validate-and-merge dispatch contains the evidence spine (15540 s) and then post-merge validation (11400 s), plus the five judge and certifier stages at their worker-policy walls (5 x 675 s) and about 900 s of setup, for a 31665 s (528 minute) floor. GitHub caps a hosted job at 360 minutes, so no value of timeout-minutes bounds it. That is a signal to MEASURE the mutation rung -- 8580 s of the 10020 s ladder is a projection with no observation behind it -- not to raise a job limit past what the platform allows. Recorded here, and in D-075, rather than papered over with a number that would not hold.
